code.originalText: Six-month review: respiratory care, skin, bladder and kidney surveillance, vaccines, and plans for the winter

text.paragraph: Six-month review: respiratory care, skin, bladder and kidney surveillance, vaccines, and plans for the winter. [S]

Mr. Reeve returns six months after his first visit. He uses the pacer for three hours twice a day and the ventilator otherwise, with no respiratory infection since intake. His skin has stayed intact. He has had no symptoms of autonomic dysreflexia. His bladder and bowel programs are working, and he has had no unplanned hospital stay. His stool immunochemical test, HIV and hepatitis C screening from the preventive visit were negative. He feels well and wants to be protected for the winter, when he plans to keep traveling. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 83.0 kg by chair scale; blood pressure 104/64, pulse 60
On the ventilator during the visit; clear; stoma and pacer lead sites clean
Intact at all pressure points; Braden score 12

Chronic incomplete C2 tetraplegia (ASIA grade C) from a traumatic spinal cord injury in a riding fall eight years ago, with partial late recovery of sensation and movement; uses a power wheelchair and has 24-hour nursing support; at risk of autonomic dysreflexia; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented injury and his physicians' published report
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented injury and the published ASIA grade.

Chronic ventilatory failure from the high cervical injury: dependent on a ventilator through a tracheostomy, with a diaphragm pacing system implanted some weeks ago and a conditioning program to lengthen time on the pacer; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented ventilator use and pacing
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented ventilator dependence.
Neurogenic bladder after spinal cord injury, managed with an indwelling catheter
S — Synthetic; expected with this level of injury. No public source describes his bladder care.
Neurogenic bowel after spinal cord injury, managed with a daily morning bowel program
S — Synthetic; expected with this level of injury. No public source describes his bowel care.

Follow-up: Hepatitis B dose 2 in one month and the second zoster dose by early in the new year. Review in three months, or the same day for fever, a chest infection, skin redness that does not fade, or autonomic dysreflexia that does not settle with the plan. [S]
